validity.researcher_notes:
EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION/DUPLICATE all check out. The wiki page's own cited sources (OPEC Annual Statistical Bulletin editions 2012/2013/2017) do name this exact pipeline, but the live opec.org URL for ASB2017 now 301-redirects to the OPEC homepage (confirmed via curl -I: 'location: https://www.opec.org') — the wiki_citations.json snapshot showing 'expected content present' for that URL predates the rot. Retrieved working Wayback Machine snapshots of ASB2013 and ASB2017 instead and read the actual gas-pipeline tables (pdftotext -layout, since url_verifier's plain-text substring check can't parse compressed PDF streams — a documented false-negative mode for this tool, confirmed manually rather than banked as a fail).

ASB2013 Table 4.10 ('Gas pipelines in OPEC Members, 2012'), Libya section, contains TWO rows for this exact connection, matching the sheet's split into 'Pipeline 1' (P1858) and 'Pipeline 2' / P6714: 'Bu–Attifel/Intesar | Mellitah Oil and Gas | 82.46 [mi] | 34 [in] | 4,134,806 | na' and 'Bu–Attifel/Intesar (103A) | Eni Oil | 82.46 | 10 | 258,425 | na'. ASB2017 Table 9.9 confirms the same 2-line system: 'Bu Attifel/Intisar (2) | Mellitha Oil & Gas, Eni Oil | 2 x 82 [mi] | 34, 10 [in]'. So P1858 (34in) and P6714 (10in) are NOT duplicates of each other — they are the correctly-split large/small lines of a genuine parallel 2-pipe bundle, exactly as OPEC's own '(2)' notation records it. Existence is solid: an international industry body (OPEC) lists this connection consistently across 3 editions spanning 2012-2016 data, and Mellitah Oil & Gas's own corporate site (mellitahog.ly/en/sites/abu-attifel-field/, fetched live, HTTP 200) independently lists 'Abu Attifel Field' (production start 1980) as one of its own operated sites, corroborating both the field's existence and the Operator attribution 'Mellitah Oil & Gas' (OPEC calls it 'Mellitah Oil and Gas' — same entity, spelling variant) — 2 independent origins (OPEC + the operator's own site), tier high.

Length: GEM's 131.96 km matches ASB2017's rounded '82 miles' (82 x 1.609344 = 131.97 km) more closely than ASB2013's more precise '82.46 miles' (= 132.71 km, ~0.75 km / 0.6% off) — minor cross-edition rounding variance, not a material disagreement, both source editions independently support ~132 km.

Diameter 34.00 in: matches both ASB2013 and ASB2017 exactly.

Capacity 4,134,806: matches ASB2013's raw number exactly, BUT the ASB2013 table header (visible in pdftotext -layout output) reads 'Capacity ... (1,000 scm/yr)' for the Libya section — i.e. the true units are THOUSANDS of scm per year, not scm/y as GEM's CapacityUnits field states. As entered, GEM's number+units combination is off by a factor of 1000 (material spec disagreement — flagging per standing rule 5, not silently passing it).

Owner1/Owner2 (Libyan National Oil Corp 50% / Eni SpA 50%): Mellitah Oil & Gas is publicly known as the NOC-Eni joint operating company, consistent with the operator being correctly identified, but I could not find an independently citable source (within this pass's access) that states the 50/50 split specifically for this pipeline rather than for Mellitah O&G generally — leaving this as unverified-but-plausible rather than fabricating support for it.

PipelineType 'transmission': consistent with how OPEC itself groups this connection alongside undisputed long-haul trunk lines (Wafa/Mellitah, Greenstream) in the same 'Main gas pipelines' table, and with how every other pipeline in this 30-row Libya roster is classified — no reclassification indicated.

fills.researcher_notes: Status inferred contextually, not literal: OPEC lists this connection in its active 'Main gas pipelines in OPEC Members' table continuously across the 2012, 2013, and 2016(2017-published) editions — a discontinued/decommissioned line would not still appear as a current operating connection. No explicit 'operating' token in the source (as expected for this kind of table), confirmed manually with pdftotext -layout since url_verifier's substring screen can't parse this PDF's text streams (documented false-negative mode).

ASB2017 Table 9.9: 'Bu Attifel/Intisar (2) | Mellitha Oil & Gas, Eni Oil | 2 x 82 [miles] | 34, 10 [in]' — 82 mi x 1.609344 = 131.97 km, matching GEM's 131.96 almost exactly. ASB2013 gives a more precise 82.46 mi (=132.71 km), a ~0.75km/0.6% cross-edition rounding variance, not material. Confirmed via pdftotext -layout on Wayback snapshots (direct opec.org URLs now 301-redirect to the homepage).

Both Bu Attifel and Intisar are well-documented Sirte Basin oil fields in OPEC's own connection naming ('Bu-Attifel/Intesar'); Mellitah's own site independently confirms it operates 'Abu Attifel Field' (production start 1980).

OPEC ASB2013 names the operator 'Mellitah Oil and Gas' for this exact connection; Mellitah's own corporate site independently lists Abu Attifel Field as one of its own operated sites — 2 independent origins.

Could not find an independently citable source (within this pass's access — no live web search, and Wikipedia has no article on Mellitah Oil & Gas) confirming the specific 50/50 NOC/Eni ownership split for this pipeline. Mellitah Oil & Gas being an NOC-Eni joint operating company is well known and consistent with the confirmed operator attribution, but leaving the owner-percentage ref unresolved rather than fabricating support for it.

summary: Confirmed real, correctly classified, and NOT a duplicate of P6714 (the two are the genuine large/small lines of one OPEC-documented 2-pipe bundle) — but Capacity is off by 1000x: OPEC's own table header reads capacity in '(1,000 scm/yr)', not the 'scm/y' GEM has recorded, and the cited ASB2017 direct link is now dead (redirects to opec.org homepage); added Wayback-verified refs for Status/Length/Location/Operator, left Owner% unresolved.
